Thought: I need to determine the conjugate base of bisulfite. 

First, let me recall what a conjugate base is. When an acid loses a proton (H+), what remains is called its conjugate base. So I need to identify what bisulfite is and what it becomes when it loses a proton.

Bisulfite is HSO3- (hydrogen sulfite ion). When it loses a proton (H+), it becomes SO3^2- (sulfite ion).

So the conjugate base of bisulfite (HSO3-) is sulfite ion (SO3^2-).

Looking at the options:
A. Sulfate ion (SO4^2-) - This is not the conjugate base of bisulfite
B. Sulfite ion (SO3^2-) - This is the conjugate base of bisulfite
C. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) - This is not the conjugate base of bisulfite
D. Thiosulfate ion (S2O3^2-) - This is not the conjugate base of bisulfite

The correct answer is B. Sulfite ion.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
